newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says U.S. dollar policy is unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says U.S. dollar policy is unchanged.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Monday that the Clinton administration's dollar policy is unchanged.

Asked at a House Judiciary Committee hearing why he did repeat the administration's often-stated position that it favors a strong dollar, Rubin explained, "I have a shorthand for that now by saying that our policies are unchanged."

Rubin also said it was his and others' belief that the Bureau of Labor Statistics' current productivity measure understates what is actually going on in the economy, particularly in the area of services.

"Productivity numbers, it seems to me, are subject to real question," he said. "There are many thoughtful people who feel that the productivity numbers substantially understate the productivity, particularly in the services sector."

Rubin, in remarks to reporters after the hearing, said, "If your question is, can we continue to have good, solid growth in per capita income, in disposable income per capita and low inflation, I think the answer is yes."

He added that the president's State of the Union address on Tuesday will make the point that the United States needs to do the things that increase productivity because that is where growth will come from.
